title: Reality survives the Fourier projection
statement:
Let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, let
$X_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\times_{k_0}\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ with second
projection $p_2:X_0\to\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ of
[def-fd-transform], and let $\mathcal K$ be a
constructible Weil sheaf on
$X_0$ which is $\iota$-real in the sense of
[def-wf-iota-real]. Assume that

$$
R^\nu p_{2,!}\mathcal K=0\qquad(\nu\neq1).
$$

Then $R^{1}p_{2,!}\mathcal K$ is $\iota$-real.

proof.text: Put $G=R^1p_{2,!}\mathcal K$. The compact-support functor of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and the bounded constructible domains of [prop-functor-package] place $Rp_{2,!}\mathcal K$ in $D^b_c(\mathbf A^1_k,\Qlb)$; its degree-one cohomology is constructible. The package's Frobenius-equivariant comparisons give the induced Weil structure on $G$. Fix a closed point $\xi$ of the target, of degree $d\geq1$, and an embedding $\kappa(\xi)\hookrightarrow k$. Write $C_0=X_0\times_{\mathbf A^1_{k_0}}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$ and $C=C_0\times_{\kappa(\xi)}k$. Thus $C_0\simeq\mathbf A^1_{\kappa(\xi)}$. Restrict $\mathcal K$ to $C$ and give it the degree-$d$ iterated Weil structure, denoting this sheaf by $L$. The datum of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] then makes $L$ a Weil sheaf over $\kappa(\xi)$, with geometric Frobenius $\gamma^d$.

source.place: Step 1: setting up the fibre and its residue-field Weil structure

proof.text:
Compact-support base change, clause (4) of [prop-functor-package], applied to the geometric point above $\xi$ identifies
$$\bigl(Rp_{2,!}\mathcal K\bigr)_{\bar\xi}\simeq R\Gamma_c(C,L).$$
The package states coherence and equivariance of these comparisons: applying the comparison to the degree-$d$ iterated Weil map intertwines the closed-point operator $F_\xi$ on the left with the compact Frobenius on the right. In the notation of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], taking degree $i$ gives
$$G_{\bar\xi}\simeq H_c^1(C,L),\qquad H_c^i(C,L)=0\ (i\ne1).$$
Here stalk cohomology is precisely the cohomology of the point-fibre complex in that definition, so the given vanishing of higher direct images gives the displayed vanishing. Functoriality then intertwines every $m$-th power as well.

source.place: Step 1: replacing the incorrect ordinary-direct-image citation by compact-support base change

proof.text: Choose a finite coefficient-field representative $(E,L_E)$, including the Weil map and its inverse, using [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]: the two maps and their inverse equations occur over one common finite extension. Choose an integral representative $L_{\mathcal O}$ of its underlying object using [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], whose scalar localization has the same objects. Its reductions $L_n$ are bounded constructible. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] these reductions have finite Tor amplitude. Apply [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) to each $L_n$ and choose a bounded constructible etale object $B_n$ and an isomorphism $\nu_C^*B_n\simeq L_n$. These are the explicit etale-origin witnesses required by the trace theorem. No invertible integral Weil structure is claimed or needed.

source.place: Step 1: checking the finite-level hypotheses of the coefficient trace theorem

proof.text: Use $C_0=\mathbf A^1_{\kappa(\xi)}\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\xi)}\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$ and geometric base change. The finite-level hypotheses spelled out in [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] include the graph correspondences of every Frobenius iterate and their fixed-point base changes. These maps, as well as the compactification maps, are separated finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes: the iterates extend to $\mathbf P^1$, their graphs and the diagonal are closed in $\mathbf P^1\times_k\mathbf P^1$, and the fixed loci are their fibre products. For each such map at every $A_{E,n}$, [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2)-(3) gives the relative adjunction and refinement comparisons, [thm-sf-ctf-stability](iv)-(v) gives both finite-Tor restrictions, and [thm-sf-preservation-class](1)-(3) gives bounds independent of $n$. These theorems apply to all these maps, not only to the structure map of $C$. Composition and base-change exchanges are the mates specified in [def-trf-admissibility] of the coherent compact-support exchanges of [prop-functor-package]. Thus the required constructible admissibility datum exists for all the trace-formula maps. No unrestricted unbounded pro-etale adjunction is used.

source.place: Step 1: discharging compactification admissibility on the constructible finite-Tor domains

proof.text:
Apply [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] over the finite field $\kappa(\xi)=\mathbf F_{q^d}$ to $L$, with the witnesses and admissibility verified in Steps 3-4. For every $m\geq1$ it gives
$$-\operatorname{Tr}(F_\xi^m\mid G_{\bar\xi})=\sum_{z\in C_0(\mathbf F_{q^{dm}})}\operatorname{Tr}(F^{L}_{z,m}\mid L_{\bar z}).$$
Step 2 identifies the global operator and removes every cohomological degree except degree one, whose sign is $-1$. The local alternating traces have just degree zero since $L$ is a sheaf. All coefficient spaces are finite-dimensional by the trace theorem, and the point set is finite by [lem-weil-point-counts-finite](1), applied with base field $\kappa(\xi)$.

source.place: Step 1: the actual coefficient trace formula, rather than constant-coefficient point counting

proof.text: To apply the orbit formula on $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, choose a finite-field representative of $\mathcal K$ with its invertible Weil map by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], and an integral representative by [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Its reductions have finite Tor amplitude by [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]. These verify the lattice hypothesis of [lem-trf-rational-local-frobenius-powers] on $X$, separately from the fibre lattice in Step 3. For a summand $z$ in Step 5 let $x\in|X_0|$ be its image and $e=[\kappa(x):k_0]$. The embedding $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow\mathbf F_{q^{dm}}$ gives $e\mid dm$. The local operator for $L$ is the degree-$dm$ operator for $\mathcal K$: grouping the $dm$ factors of the iterated Weil map into $m$ groups of $d$ factors, and the corresponding point transports in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], gives the same composite. By [lem-trf-rational-local-frobenius-powers] this is conjugate to $F_x^{dm/e}$, first over a finite coefficient field and then over $\Qlb$. By [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws](1),(4), its trace is therefore $\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^{dm/e}\mid\mathcal K_{\bar x})$. No invertible integral Weil map is required.

source.place: Steps 1-2: correcting the local closed-point exponent

proof.text:
Fix such a closed point $x$. By [def-wf-iota-real], the polynomial $P_x(T)=\iota\det(1-TF_x)$ has real coefficients and constant coefficient $1$. By [lem-weil-exp-trace-determinant] and the finite coefficient formulas of [def-weil-power-series-exponential], put
$$S_x=\sum_{r\geq1}s_rT^r,\quad s_r=\iota\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^r)/r,\qquad E_x=\exp(S_x)=P_x^{-1}.$$
All coefficients $b_n$ of $E_x$ are real: writing $P_x=1+\sum_{j\geq1}a_jT^j$, the inverse identity gives $b_0=1$ and $b_n=-\sum_{j=1}^na_jb_{n-j}$. The displayed exponential coefficient formula gives $b_n=s_n+Q_n(s_1,\ldots,s_{n-1})$, where $Q_n$ is the finite sum with $2\leq r\leq n$ from that formula and has rational coefficients. Induction on $n\geq1$ therefore makes each $s_n$ real, and multiplying by $n$ makes every $\iota\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^n)$ real. The case of a zero-dimensional stalk has $P_x=E_x=1$ and the same recursion gives zero traces.

source.place: Step 2: real local factors imply real power traces, expanding Newton recovery by coefficient recursions

proof.text: Apply Step 7 with exponent $dm/e$ to each summand identified in Step 6. The point set in Step 5 is finite, so its sum is real after $\iota$; its negative is real too. Thus $t_m=\iota\operatorname{Tr}(F_\xi^m\mid G_{\bar\xi})$ is real for every $m\geq1$. This includes an empty sum and includes a zero stalk.

Apply [lem-weil-exp-trace-determinant] to the finite-dimensional stalk $G_{\bar\xi}$ and its operator $F_\xi$. With $P=\iota\det(1-TF_\xi)$ it gives
$$P\exp\Bigl(\sum_{m\geq1}t_mT^m/m\Bigr)=1.$$
Every coefficient $b_n$ of this exponential is real, since the formula in [def-weil-power-series-exponential] expresses it as a finite sum of products of the real numbers $t_m/m$ divided by factorials. If $P=\sum a_nT^n$, the product identity gives $a_0=b_0=1$ and $a_n=-\sum_{j=1}^nb_ja_{n-j}$; induction makes each $a_n$ real. Hence $\iota\det(1-TF_\xi)\in\mathbf R[T]$. Since $\xi$ was arbitrary, [def-wf-iota-real] gives the asserted reality of $G$. The recursions need no semisimplicity or nonzero rank.

proof_origin.place: Steps 1-3, with corrected citations, verified trace hypotheses and elementary coefficient recursions
